Q: How to get config/utility files of vim in SUSE Linux A:

First, the files and directories under $VIMRUNTIME are support files that Vim needs to run properly. You are not supposed to edit, delete, add, or move anything, there. You are not even supposed to look at it, really. Not because it is proprietary or anything like that, but because:

  • it could break Vim, this is exactly what is happening to you,
  • nothing there is particularly relevant unless you are pretty advanced,
  • it's system-level stuff anyway so it's off limits by design.

I don't know SUSE but David C. Rankin's advice seems sound. You should probably follow it to get back a usable Vim.

Now, configuring Vim is done in your $HOME directory, by way of a vimrc file and a .vim directory. Whatever you want to do to customize Vim, it should never be done elsewhere.

Your configuration file:

$HOME/.vimrc

is where you put things like:

syntax on
colorscheme zaibatsu
…

And your runtime directory:

$HOME/.vim/

is where you put third-party plugins, syntax scripts, etc.

I have a more complete write-up on the subject over there.

Q: RavenDb with error when saving entity with id as Guid A:

RavenDB document IDs must always be strings.
They cannot be stored or generated as Guid fields on the entity.
Even if the value is a GUID, it must still be a string.

See:
https://docs.ravendb.net/7.2/server/kb/document-identifier-generation
https://docs.ravendb.net/7.2/client-api/document-identifiers/working-with-document-identifiers

Q: Unable to load admin styles in a WordPress block plugin A:

To load styles in the WordPress admin area, make sure you are using the correct hook.

For admin-specific styles, you should use the `admin_enqueue_scripts` action instead of `wp_enqueue_scripts`.

Example:
function myplugin_enqueue_admin_styles( $hook ) {

wp_enqueue_style(
'myplugin-admin-style',
plugin_dir_url( _FILE_ ) . 'admin.css',
array(),
'1.0'
);
}
add_action( 'admin_enqueue_scripts', 'myplugin_enqueue_admin_styles' );

Also ensure that:

- The CSS file path is correct

- The plugin is active

- There are no PHP errors preventing the hook from running

This approach ensures admin styles are loaded correctly without affecting the frontend.

Q: How can I run older Xcode version on new macOS version? A:

⚠️ Important:

  • This does not work on macOS 15.4

  • Do not update to macOS 15.4 if you want to keep using old Xcode

Change the paths to OLD/NEW Xcodes and run the script. The script will change the build version of the old Xcode to the new one, run it, and restore it. The script needs to be run once; after that, Xcode can be opened via double-click.

P.S. The old Xcode should be from https://developer.apple.com/download/, not from the App Store.

Works on macOS Monterey for Xcode 12.5.1, Ventura for Xcode 13, Sonoma for Xcode 14, Sequoia for Xcode 15.

#!/bin/sh

set -euo pipefail

# Set the paths to your Old/New Xcodes
OLD_XCODE="/Applications/Xcode_14.3.1.app" # or /Applications/Xcode_13.4.1.app on Ventura
NEW_XCODE="/Applications/Xcode.app" # To get build number

# Get New Xcode build number
OLD_XCODE_BUILD=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print CFBundleVersion" ${OLD_XCODE}/Contents/Info.plist)
NEW_XCODE_BUILD=$(/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print CFBundleVersion" ${NEW_XCODE}/Contents/Info.plist)

echo The Old Xcode build version is $OLD_XCODE_BUILD
echo The New Xcode build version is $NEW_XCODE_BUILD

# Change Old Xcode build version to New Xcode
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :CFBundleVersion ${NEW_XCODE_BUILD}" ${OLD_XCODE}/Contents/Info.plist

# Open Old Xcode (system will check build version and cache it)
open $OLD_XCODE || true

# Revert Old's Xcode's build version
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :CFBundleVersion ${OLD_XCODE_BUILD}" ${OLD_XCODE}/Contents/Info.plist
